commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add LarperBoard non-functional requirements
commitResults.messageBody:
The NFR section still held the three AB3 defaults and a placeholder.

Replace them with 19 requirements covering environment, performance,
capacity, usability, offline use, privacy, data, reliability, display,
scope and maintainability. Each is tied to the hackathon target user
and stated so that it can be tested.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add LinkedIn class to represent a person's LinkedIn handle
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts met at hackathons are usually followed up with on LinkedIn,
but a person has no field to store a LinkedIn handle.

Add a LinkedIn value class that accepts letters, digits and hyphens,
3 to 50 characters long. An empty value represents the absence of a
handle, as the field is optional.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add optional LinkedIn field to Person
commitResults.messageBody:
The LinkedIn class exists but is not used, so users cannot record a
contact's LinkedIn handle.

Let's
* accept an optional l/LINKEDIN_HANDLE in the add and edit commands,
  where an empty l/ in edit clears the handle
* save the handle in the data file, treating a missing field as no
  handle so that existing data files still load
* show the handle in the person card and in command results only when
  a person has one
* update the User Guide

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for LinkedIn display and formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
The LinkedIn handling in PersonCard, Messages#format and
Person#hashCode is not exercised by any test.

Add tests for them. PersonCardTest needs the JavaFX toolkit, so it is
skipped in environments without a display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Add optional LinkedIn field to contacts

Contacts have a compulsory address, but LarperBoard's target users
(hackathon participants) do not need one, and it blocks adding a
contact with only a name.

Let's,
* delete the Address class and the a/ prefix
* drop address from Person, add and edit parsing, storage and the
  person card

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Remove address from test data and utilities
commitResults.messageBody:
Address was removed from Person, so tests, builders and JSON fixtures
that referenced it no longer compile or reflect the product.

Let's,
* delete AddressTest and the address helpers in test utilities
* drop address-only cases from parser, storage and model tests
* strip "address" from the JSON test fixtures
* add a test that a legacy data file with an address field still loads

Phone numbers have a 3-digit minimum but no maximum, so arbitrarily
long digit strings are accepted as phone numbers.

Let's,
* cap the validation regex at 20 digits
* update the constraint message to state the 3-20 digit range
* add boundary tests for 20 and 21 digits

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Remove address from edit and data sections
commitResults.messageBody:

* drop a/ADDRESS from the edit format
* rename AddressBook to LarperBoard in the edit, saving, data file

* note that a legacy address field in the data file is ignored
Limit phone numbers to 3-20 digits
Update UG: edit command and data file sections

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Add LarperBoard glossary terms
commitResults.messageBody:
The glossary only contains two terms inherited from AddressBook,
one of which is not used anywhere in the Developer Guide, so readers
have no definitions for the terms specific to LarperBoard.

Replace the unused term and define the terms used in the user stories
and use cases, such as contact, tag, note, archive and export, so the
guide is understandable without prior knowledge of the product.
Developer Guide: Add LarperBoard glossary terms

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Refine target user and value proposition
commitResults.messageBody:
The target user profile and value proposition do not yet mention
that users find saving contacts on a phone too much effort during an
event, forget many contacts afterwards, or may have unreliable
internet at crowded venues.

Add these points so that the profile matches the persona and the
user stories, and rewrite the value proposition to lead with the
outcome and mention that data is stored locally.
Developer Guide: Refine target user and value proposition

commitResults.messageTitle: Add view command to show a person's details
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can only see a compact summary of each person in the list,
and there is no command to look at a single person on its own.

Add the view command, which takes the index of a person in the
displayed list and shows that person's details in the result
display. An invalid index is rejected in the same way as for the
delete command. The detail panel will be added in a later change.
Add view command

The view command reports a generic format error when the user gives
more than one index or an index larger than the integer limit, and
reports an invalid index when the person list is empty. The delete
command already reports each of these cases specifically.

Show the same specific messages as the delete command for multiple
indexes and for an oversized index, and show that the person list is
empty when there is nobody to view.
Handle view command edge cases

commitResults.messageTitle: Add detail panel for the view command
commitResults.messageBody:
The view command shows the viewed person as a single line of text in
the result display.

This is hard to read when a person has many tags, and it disappears as
soon as the next command is run.

Let's add a detail panel next to the person list that shows the name,
phone, email, LinkedIn handle and tags of the viewed person, and shows
that no contact is selected until a person is viewed.

The model keeps track of the viewed person so that the panel can follow
it without the UI having to know about the view command. The minimum
window width is raised from 450 to 700 to fit the panel.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add LogicManager tests for the viewed person
commitResults.messageBody:
The LogicManager method that exposes the viewed person to the UI is
not exercised by any test.

Add tests that check that no person is viewed at the start and that
the viewed person is the one selected by the view command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add MainWindow test for the detail panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The code that adds the detail panel to the main window is not
exercised by any test, so a mistake in how the panel is wired up
would go unnoticed.

Add a test that builds the main window and checks that the detail panel
is part of it and shows the person selected by the view command.
Add detail panel for the view command

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep detail panel in sync with the contact list
commitResults.messageBody:
The detail panel keeps showing the viewed person after that person
has been edited, tagged or deleted, or after the address book has been
cleared, so it can show details that are out of date or no longer exist.

Let's make the model update the viewed person whenever it replaces or
removes that person, and clear it when all data is replaced, so the
panel shows the updated contact or goes back to showing that no contact
is selected.

The default window is 740 by 600, which is too small now that the
main window shows the person list and the detail panel side by side.

Change the default to 900 by 720, so that the person list keeps its
width and the detail panel has room for the details of a contact.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Add view command section
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not describe the view command or the detail panel
that it fills, so users cannot find out how to see all the details of
a person.

Add a section for view with its format, what the detail panel shows,
examples and the error messages, together with a screenshot of the
panel, and add view to the command summary.
Keep detail panel in sync with the contact list
Enlarge default window size

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag class: Enforce canonical tag validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags accept only alphanumeric characters and preserve input casing,
with no maximum length.

The tagging MVP requires hyphens and plus signs, a 1 to 20 character
limit, and case-insensitive behavior.

Let's enforce the validation rules, normalize tags to lowercase, and add
tests covering the required behavior.
Tag class: Enforce canonical tag validation

Support adding one or more tags to a person while preserving
their existing tags, with parser and command test coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge team master into tag command branch
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag command branch needs the team's v1.3 changes to resolve PR
conflicts. Bring in the view command, detail panel, LinkedIn support,
and address removal. Preserve both tag and view parsing, and update
tagging and its tests to retain LinkedIn details.

Adding an existing tag replaces the person needlessly, and an
oversized index produces a generic format error. Keep duplicate tags
as a no-op, report index overflow consistently with delete and view,
and test filtered-list targeting, equality, and hash codes.
Add tag command

Tag commands give inconsistent feedback for invalid person indexes, and
several input edge cases lack focused test coverage.

Report the person-index error for zero, negative, non-numeric, and
out-of-range indexes. Add parser and command tests for missing or invalid
tags and case-insensitive duplicates, while preserving the usage message
when the tag parameter is missing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align index errors across person commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Delete and view report different errors from tag for invalid person
indexes. The duplicate-tag command test also depends on the parser.

Use the same person-index error across all three commands while keeping
usage feedback for missing indexes. Construct the duplicate-tag command
directly so its test covers command behavior independently.
Handle tag command edge cases

commitResults.messageTitle: Update User Guide for v1.3 commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide omits tag and view, and its command summary does not
cover all released commands. Several rules, error messages, and
screenshots also describe older behavior, which can mislead users
following the v1.3 release.

Document tag syntax, validation, additive updates, and duplicate
handling. Add the view command and complete the command summary.
Correct add and delete guidance, help output, and save behavior to
match the parser and model.

Use consistent contact terminology and remove guide references to
screenshots showing obsolete fields and an old help URL. Preserve
the actual data-file path so users can locate their saved contacts.
